_notes: The BILLING PORTAL (:8446) is a separate Keycloak client from the dashboard.
Realm is still `masar`, but the client is `billing-portal`, not `masar-dashboard` — confirmed
from the portal's own /runtime-env.js. Same realm means the SSO cookie is shared, so a browser
already signed in to :8444 lands here without re-entering a password.
The portal has its own API base too: https://192.168.225.195:8446/masar-service/api/v1
(EPTTS_BILLING_API_URL). It is NOT the :8444 masar-service, and billing endpoints are only
served here.
LOGGED IN AS THE MANUFACTURER, DELIBERATELY.
The billing portal is role-scoped, and the role changes what exists on the page rather than
just what is enabled. As a manufacturer the nav has three items (Dashboard, Unbilled
Operations, Invoices); as Platform Admin it has five (adding Reports and Configuration).
More importantly, the per-invoice `💰 Pay` action ONLY renders for the MAH that owes the
invoice — an admin never sees it. Discovery done as admin therefore recorded the Invoices row
actions as Details/CSV/PDF and missed the entire payment surface. Cases that need the admin
view (billing mode, manual payment, bank-transfer approval) build their own state instead.
NO DISCLAIMER AND NO LANGUAGE STEP HERE.
The production-access disclaimer modal is a :8444 component (app-disclaimer-modal) and does
not exist on this portal. The language control is a <select> labelled `Language`, not the
:8444 `EN` button, and it already reads English on load — so there is nothing to switch and
login-config.ts's step vocabulary (which has no selectOption action) is sufficient as-is.
ON 2FA: THE OTP REQUIREMENT WAS REMOVED FROM THE DEVSIM ACCOUNTS ON 2026-09-08.
Until then every live account (janssen2@masar.com, and the admin) answered the password step
with a One-time code prompt, which no declarative step can satisfy -- auth.setup.ts timed out
and wrote EMPTY_STATE every run. It is gone now, verified by this flow completing unattended,
so the normal path works again and specs use stateFor('<slug>').
If it ever comes back, the fallback is already built rather than needing rediscovery:
node automation-hub/scripts/capture-state.mjs --portal <slug> --role admin
writes .auth/<slug>-<role>.json, which auth.setup.ts does not own and cannot overwrite, and
lib/captured-state.ts reads it with an actionable error when it is missing or stale. An admin
capture is also mirrored onto .auth/<slug>.json so existing projects keep working.
